records.name: SAS Date Value Numeric Addition (+ n days)

interpretation.description: In SAS DATA step, `new_date = old_date + 30;` adds 30 days because SAS date unit is integer days.
interpretation.missing_behavior: If old_date is missing (.), new_date becomes missing (.)

validation_rules: In Python datetime.date, `old_date + 30` raises TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'datetime.date' and 'int'
Target correction in Python must be: `old_date + datetime.timedelta(days=30)`

records.name: SAS Datetime Value Numeric Addition (+ n seconds)

interpretation.description: In SAS DATA step, `new_dt = old_dt + 30;` adds 30 SECONDS, not 30 days! To add 30 days to a SAS datetime, code must do `old_dt + (30 * 86400)` or use INTNX.

validation_rules: Distinguish date addition (days) from datetime addition (seconds)

records.name: SAS INTNX Function (Interval Date Calculation)

interpretation.description: INTNX(interval, start-from, increment, alignment). Calculates date at start/middle/end of interval.
interpretation.python_equivalent: Requires dateutil.relativedelta or pandas DateOffset (e.g. pd.DateOffset(months=1))

validation_rules: Do not replace INTNX('month', dt, 1) with timedelta(days=30) because calendar months have 28, 29, 30, or 31 days
